` has **no** flagged cross-iteration dependence at all (its write index `ju[i]` and its two read indices `ju[i]`/`ku[i]` never alias across iterations in the profile), so `u`'s accesses are safe to leave exactly as they are, in the same order, with the same index expressions.

**Why buffering/reordering is not safe here.** Since this is a single sweep (the function runs once) and DiscoPoP *dynamically observed* the v-RAW as real, a Jacobi-style rewrite that reads `v` from a pre-loop snapshot would silently drop the intra-sweep update some later iteration is supposed to see — that would change output. Likewise splitting into two full loops (all `u` updates, then all `v` updates) would make `v[jv[i]] += u[ku[i]] * d[i]` read the *final* `u` array instead of the value visible at iteration `i` in program order, again changing results. So the fix cannot reorder or buffer around this dependence; it must preserve the exact original sequence of reads/writes on `v` and `u`.

**What I changed.** I did not alter any index expression, loop bound, or the relative order of memory operations (so no bound needed re-deriving — the sweep still runs `i = 1 .. LEN_1D-1` in the same order, touching the same elements in the same sequence). I only made the two-stage producer/consumer structure explicit: stage 1 loads `v[kv[i]]` into a local and updates `u[ju[i]]` (self-contained per iteration, since `u` never aliases across iterations); stage 2 loads `u[ku[i]]` and performs the single store to `v[jv[i]]` that is the actual carrier of the cross-iteration dependence, isolated as the last action of the iteration. This is a behavior-preserving refactor (identical values, identical order) that exposes the true single edge of loop-carried dependence (v, stage 2 → later iteration's stage 1) as a clean two-stage pipeline shape for DiscoPoP's re-profiling, rather than leaving it embedded in two compound-assignment statements that mix a safe access (`u`) with the one genuinely carried access (`v`).
